instructions: Deploy at paranoia level 1. Detects classic OR/AND 1=1 boolean bypass patterns after normalization. Removed triple urlDecodeUni (two passes sufficient after htmlEntityDecode), removed possessive quantifiers and capture flag for compatibility.

Deploy at paranoia level 1. Detects UNION SELECT combined with common exfiltration targets such as user(), version(), @@version, information_schema. Removed trailing anchor group as pattern already constrains matching sufficiently.
Deploy at paranoia level 1. Detects sleep(), benchmark(), and nested select-sleep time-delay patterns used in blind SQLi. Simplified alternation order for clarity and performance.

Deploy at paranoia level 2. Detects SQL keywords followed by comment terminators used for obfuscation. Removed the standalone trailing-comment-only branch (--|# at end of string) which was too broad and caused false positives on legitimate URLs with fragments. Kept the keyword+comment combo which has higher confidence.

Deploy at paranoia level 2 as a detection/logging rule (pass action). Six or more consecutive percent-encoded sequences are anomalous. Simplified pattern from original which had overlapping double-encoding branches already covered by urlDecodeUni in other rules. Monitor and tune threshold before switching to deny.

rule: SecRule ARGS|REQUEST_URI|REQUEST_BODY|REQUEST_COOKIES|REQUEST_HEADERS "@rx (?i)(?:%u[0-9a-f]{4}|%[0-9a-f]{2}|&#(?:x[0-9a-f]+|[0-9]+);)" "id:910105,phase:2,deny,status:403,log,auditlog,t:none,t:lowercase,msg:'Encoded input containing SQLi keywords after normalization',tag:'attack-evasion',tag:'attack-sqli',severity:'ERROR',chain"
instructions: Deploy at paranoia level 2. First rule of chained pair: matches any encoded character form (%uXXXX, %XX, HTML entity). Chain continues to keyword check. Removed redundant urlDecodeUni transforms from chain head since the MATCHED_VAR is the raw encoded value; keyword check is applied on the decoded form in chain rule.
Chain continuation for rule 910105. Applies decoding transforms to the matched variable and checks for SQLi keywords. Deploy immediately after rule 910105 with no ID (chain secondary rule).

Deploy at paranoia level 2. Detects admin-specific boolean bypass patterns such as admin' OR 1=1. More specific than rule 910100 and provides targeted coverage for credential stuffing via SQLi. Normalized username capture group to non-capturing for performance.
